LLC or S‑Corp — which saves you more money?

The way your business is set up changes how much tax you pay. Answer two simple questions and see which setup could save you more — and by how much.

By JK Accounting Group · For business owners in the US

Built with JuliaFounder · speaks your language

Try it with your numbers

Nothing is saved and no email is needed. You will see your answer right away.

$

After your business costs, before you pay yourself.

Please enter how much your business earns.

$

If you hired someone to do your job, what would you pay them for the year? An S‑Corp owner must take a fair salary first.

Please enter a fair salary (it cannot be more than what the business earns).

Takes about a minute.

Your estimate

As an LLC, you pay
Self‑employment tax on your whole profit.
As an S‑Corp, you pay
The same tax, but only on your salary.
See if this is right for you — book a free call → A 20‑minute call. No cost, no pressure.

What this really means

In plain words, so you can decide with your eyes open.

  • Self‑employment tax is 15.3%. It pays for Social Security and Medicare when you work for yourself. Everyone who runs a business pays it.
  • An S‑Corp splits your money in two. You take a fair salary, and the rest is business profit. You pay that 15.3% on the salary — but not on the rest. That is where the saving comes from.
  • It is not free. An S‑Corp costs a little more to run — payroll and an extra tax return, usually a few thousand dollars a year. That is why it is worth checking your real numbers before you change anything.

Send us your details and we will get back to you — in English, Russian, or Ukrainian. Or book a free 20‑minute call right away.

  • We tell you if an S‑Corp is worth it — even if the answer is "not yet."
